subtitle: How Jain courts forged an epic tongue in stone and song

cast: Ranna, Jewel of the Jain Poets
panels.shot: low-angle medium shot of a lone poet on a rocky hill, palm-leaf manuscript in hand, the great Gomaṭeśvara of Śravaṇabeḷagola rising behind him in twilight
panels.action: Ranna, Jewel of the Jain Poets stands poised on a granite slope, wind tugging his cloth and hair, as the colossal serene figure of Bahubali towers behind him under a darkening Deccan sky.

dialogue.text: In an age when kings prayed in Sanskrit, Jain poets like Ranna dared to dream in Kannada, and turned a regional tongue into a language of heroes, renouncers and empire.

i18n.hi: जब राजा संस्कृत में प्रार्थना करते थे, तब रण्णा जैसे जैन कवि कन्नड़ में सपने बुनते रहे, और इस बोली को वीरों, त्यागियों और साम्राज्य की भाषा बना डाला।

panels.shot: slow aerial sweep over the Deccan, from the Godavari plains to the hills of Karnataka, fading between temples, courts and Jain basadis
panels.action: A vast bird’s-eye view shows the tenth-century Deccan: copper-lit fields, walled towns, hilltop temples and Jain basadis, with roads like thin threads between Vemulavada, Manyakheta and the greener lands of Gangavadi.

dialogue.text: Around the mid-tenth century, the Deccan hummed with dynasties and tongues—Rashtrakutas at Manyakheta, Vemulavada Chalukyas in the east, Western Gangas in Gangavadi—and Sanskrit still claimed the throne of high speech.

i18n.hi: दसवीं सदी के बीचोंबीच दक्खन राजवंशों और बोलियों से गूंज रहा था—मण्यखेड़ा में राष्ट्रकूट, पूरब में विमुलवाड़ा चालुक्य, गंगवाड़ी में पश्चिमी गंगा—और ऊँची ज़बान की गद्दी पर अभी भी संस्कृत बैठी थी।

panels.shot: intimate interior wide shot of a Jain basadi library lit by oil lamps, palm-leaf bundles stacked high
panels.action: Inside a Jain basadi, monks and lay-scholars sit cross-legged amid shelves of palm-leaf manuscripts, fine stylus marks gleaming under lamp-light, as a teacher gestures to both Sanskrit and Kannada texts laid before his students.

dialogue.text: In the Jain basadis, however, another current gathered strength: monks copied Brahmi letters into Kannada scripts, students recited Prakrit gathas, and lay patrons listened as stories of Tirthankaras were retold in their own speech.

i18n.hi: पर जैन बसदियों में एक और धारा ताकत जुटा रही थी: भिक्षु ब्राह्मी को कन्नड़ लिपि में उतारते, विद्यार्थी प्राकृत गाथाएँ रटते, और श्रावक तीरथंकरों की कथाएँ अपनी ही बोली में सुनते।

panels.shot: medium shot of a court scene in Vemulavada, with Pampa reciting before a seated king
panels.action: In a richly pillared hall, the poet Pampa stands before the Vemulavada Chalukya king Arikesari II, one hand raised in recitation, while courtiers lean in and a palm-leaf manuscript of Adipurana rests open beside him.

dialogue.text: In 941, at Vemulavada, Pampa completed his Adipurana and Vikramarjuna Vijaya, proving that Kannada could carry both the cosmic spans of a Jina’s life and the martial glory of an Arjuna-like king.

i18n.hi: ९४१ में विमुलवाड़ा में पम्पा ने आदि पुराण और विक्रम अर्जुन विजय पूरा किया, दिखा दिया कि कन्नड़ में जीन के विराट जीवन से लेकर अर्जुन जैसे नरेश की वीरता तक सब समा सकता है।

panels.shot: courtly wide shot in a Rashtrakuta hall, with Ponna presenting a manuscript to a royal patron
panels.action: In the Rashtrakuta court at Manyakheta, the Jain poet Ponna bows, offering a neatly tied palm-leaf bundle to his seated royal patron, as other learned men in the assembly whisper and exchange impressed glances.

dialogue.text: Ponna moved through Rashtrakuta circles, hailed in inscription and memory as a master of Shantipurana, blending ethical sermons with polished courtly Kannada for listeners who once expected only Sanskrit.

i18n.hi: पोन्ना राष्ट्रकूट दरबारों में घूमते, शांति पुराण के उस्ताद के रूप में शिलालेखों और स्मृति में गाए गए, जो धर्मोपदेश को निखरी दरबारी कन्नड़ में पिरोकर उन श्रोताओं तक लाते जो कल तक सिर्फ संस्कृत की चाह रखते थे।

cast: Ranna, Jewel of the Jain Poets
panels.shot: medium close-up of young Ranna in a modest Jain household, tracing letters on a tablet
panels.action: A young Ranna sits in a simple Jain home, tracing Kannada letters on a wax-coated board with a stylus while an elder looks on, and in the background a small shrine with a seated Tirthankara glows faintly.

dialogue.text: Into this world was born Ranna, a Jain layman of Karnataka, learning his first letters under the watchful gaze of both elders and images of the Jinas, hearing that Pampa and Ponna had already raised Kannada high.

i18n.hi: इसी दुनिया में जन्मा रण्णा, कर्नाटक का जैन श्रावक; बूढ़ों और जीन प्रतिमाओं की निगाह में अक्षर सीखता, सुनता कि पम्पा–पोन्ना कन्नड़ को पहले ही ऊँचाई पर पहुँचा चुके हैं।

cast: Ranna, Jewel of the Jain Poets
panels.shot: wide shot of Shravanabelagola hill with pilgrims and scholars, Ranna in the crowd
panels.action: From a distance we see Shravanabelagola’s twin hills with their steps carved in stone, pilgrims ascending with offerings, and among them a slightly older Ranna pausing halfway up, sweating yet awed by the looming Gomaṭeśvara.

dialogue.text: At Shravanabelagola, the Western Ganga stronghold of Jain piety, stone hills, basadis and the colossal Bahubali drew scholars and patrons together, and Ranna’s steps joined this flow of devotion and learning.

i18n.hi: श्रवणबेलगोला में, जैन भक्ति के गंगा दुर्ग पर, पत्थर की टेकड़ियाँ, बसदियाँ और विराट बाहुबली विद्वानों और दानियों को खींच लाते, और इसी भक्ति–विद्या की धारा में रण्णा के कदम भी जुड़ जाते।

cast: Ranna, Jewel of the Jain Poets
panels.shot: interior medium shot in a Ganga noble’s hall, Chavundaraya listening as Ranna recites
panels.action: In a dignified hall with Western Ganga emblems on the pillars, Ranna stands respectfully before the noble Chavundaraya, holding a palm-leaf as he recites, while Chavundaraya listens, chin in hand, surrounded by Jain monks and courtiers.

dialogue.text: Inscription and tradition remember Ranna among those linked to Chavundaraya, the great Ganga general and patron, whose own commissioning of Jain works created the very circles in which Kannada letters could thrive.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख और परंपरा रण्णा को चावुंडराय से जोड़ते हैं—महान गंगा सेनापति और दाता—जिनके जैन ग्रंथों के उपक्रम ने वही गोष्ठियाँ रचीं जिनमें कन्नड़ लेखन फल-फूल सका।

cast: Ranna, Jewel of the Jain Poets
panels.shot: close-up on Ranna’s face, torn between two manuscripts—one Sanskrit, one Kannada
panels.action: Ranna sits alone in a quiet corner, a Sanskrit manuscript opened on one side and a Kannada text on the other, his brows furrowed as lamplight flickers between the two scripts, his fingers hovering over the Kannada lines.

dialogue.speaker: Ranna, Jewel of the Jain Poets
dialogue.text: Can our own tongue bear the weight of Bhima’s courage and the Jinas’ truth?

i18n.hi: क्या हमारी अपनी ज़बान भी भीम की वीरता और जीनों की सच्चाई उठा सकती है?

cast: Ranna, Jewel of the Jain Poets
panels.shot: medium shot of Ranna composing, with an image of Ajitha or a Tirthankara before him
panels.action: Ranna writes intently on palm leaves, his stylus moving steadily as a small bronze image of a Tirthankara sits before him, incense curling upward, the open leaf titled mentally toward Ajitha Purana in his mind.

dialogue.text: Ranna’s first known work, Ajitha Purana, retold the life of the second Tirthankara, Ajitanatha, in Kannada, bringing a Jina’s calm renunciation into the earthy rhythm of a tongue spoken in markets and courts.

i18n.hi: रण्णा का पहला ज्ञात ग्रंथ अजित पुराण, दूसरे तीर्थंकर अजितनाथ का जीवन कन्नड़ में कहता है, जीन का शांत वैराग्य बाज़ारों और दरबारों में बोली जाने वाली ज़बान की मिट्टी भरी लय में उतारता है।

cast: Ranna, Jewel of the Jain Poets
panels.shot: dynamic low-angle shot of Ranna narrating a battle scene from Sahasa Bhima Vijaya to an attentive mixed audience
panels.action: Ranna stands animated before a mixed audience of warriors, merchants and monks, gesturing as if to show Bhima’s mace blow, while listeners lean forward, caught between the martial excitement and the Jain ethic beneath his tale.

dialogue.text: With Sahasa Bhima Vijaya, also known as Gadayuddha, Ranna cast the Mahabharata’s mace-duel into Kannada, yet under Jain patronage he shaped Bhima’s courage within a frame that still remembered restraint and karma.

i18n.hi: साहस भीम विजय, यानी गदायुद्ध में, रण्णा ने महाभारत के गदा–समर को कन्नड़ में ढाला; पर जैन दान से वे भीम की वीरता को ऐसे फ़्रेम में रखते हैं जहाँ संयम और कर्म की याद बाकी रहती है।

cast: Ranna, Jewel of the Jain Poets
panels.shot: medium shot in a later Chalukya court, king Satyashraya honoring Ranna before assembled nobles
panels.action: In a later Western Chalukya court, King Satyashraya sits on a carved throne as Ranna stands crowned with a garland, courtiers clapping softly, a court scribe nearby noting the honor in Kannada on a fresh palm leaf.

dialogue.text: Ranna’s fame spread; under the later Chalukyas he was honored as a jewel among poets, proof that a writer shaped in Jain-Ganga circles could now stand at the heart of a royal Kannada cosmopolis.

i18n.hi: रण्णा की कीर्ति फैल गई; उत्तर चालुक्यों के राज में उन्हें कवियों के रत्न की मान मिला, सबूत कि जैन–गंगा गोष्ठियों में तपे लेखक अब राजसी कन्नड़ लोक में केंद्र तक पहुँच सकते हैं।

cast: Ranna, Jewel of the Jain Poets
panels.shot: quiet wide shot of Ranna and his patron Attimabbe overseeing the copying of manuscripts
panels.action: In a shaded courtyard, the noblewoman Attimabbe supervises a line of scribes carefully copying Ranna’s works onto palm leaves, while Ranna stands beside her, humbly indicating corrections as bundles of finished manuscripts pile up.

dialogue.text: Later inscriptions praise Attimabbe for having hundreds of Kannada copies of Jain texts made and gifted, showing how women patrons and scribes carried Ranna’s words far beyond the courts that first heard them.

i18n.hi: बाद के शिलालेख अत्तिमब्बे की सराहना करते हैं कि उन्होंने जैन ग्रंथों की सैकड़ों कन्नड़ प्रतियाँ बनवाकर दान कीं, दिखाते हैं कि स्त्री दानी और लिखारियाँ रण्णा के शब्दों को उन दरबारों से बहुत दूर तक ले गईं जहाँ वे पहले गूँजे थे।

cast: Ranna, Jewel of the Jain Poets
panels.shot: montage-style wide shot blending three scenes: Pampa at Vemulavada, Ponna at Manyakheta, Ranna in Karnataka, all linked by flowing Kannada script
panels.action: A composite image shows Pampa reciting at Vemulavada, Ponna debating in the Rashtrakuta court, and Ranna writing in a Karnataka basadi, all three joined by a flowing band of Kannada script weaving across the frame.

dialogue.text: The three gems—Pampa in Vemulavada, Ponna in Rashtrakuta halls, Ranna in Jain-Ganga and Chalukya circles—did not sit together at one Ganga court, yet their works shared a network of faith, patronage and language.

i18n.hi: ये तीन रत्न—विमुलवाड़ा के पम्पा, राष्ट्रकूट सभाओं के पोन्ना, और जैन–गंगा व चालुक्य गोष्ठियों के रण्णा—भले एक ही गंगा दरबार में साथ न बैठे हों, पर उनके ग्रंथ विश्वास, दान और भाषा के एक ही जाल में जुड़ते हैं।

cast: Ranna, Jewel of the Jain Poets
panels.shot: close-up of a stone inscription mentioning Ranna and Jain patrons, with Ranna’s faint reflection on the polished stone
panels.action: The camera lingers on a chiseled stone inscription that records honors to Ranna and his Jain patrons; the polished stone faintly reflects Ranna’s aging face as he reads, hands folded, in the temple courtyard.

dialogue.text: Epigraphs carved in stone remember these ties: gifts of land to basadis, praise for poets, the naming of works—evidence that Kannada’s literary rise was anchored not only in imagination but in endowments and institutions.

i18n.hi: पत्थर पर उकेरे लेख इन रिश्तों को सँजोते हैं: बसदियों को भूमि दान, कवियों की स्तुति, ग्रंथों के नाम—सब बताते हैं कि कन्नड़ का साहित्यिक उभार सिर्फ कल्पना से नहीं, दान और संस्थाओं की जड़ों से भी बंधा था।

panels.shot: wide shot of a present-day library table with old palm-leaf manuscripts of Pampa, Ponna and Ranna laid out together
panels.action: On a modern wooden table, carefully preserved palm-leaf manuscripts labeled with the names of Pampa, Ponna and Ranna lie side by side, their edges darkened, as a researcher’s hand hovers above, tracing the Kannada lines with reverence.

dialogue.text: Today, when scholars open the palm leaves of Adipurana, Shantipurana and Sahasa Bhima Vijaya, they see how a Jain literary ecology, sustained by Ganga and other courts, slowly shifted Kannada from margin to epic center.

i18n.hi: आज जब विद्वान आदि पुराण, शांति पुराण और साहस भीम विजय के ताड़पत्र खोलते हैं, वे देखते हैं कैसे गंगा और दूसरे दरबारों से सिंची जैन साहित्य–परंपरा ने धीरे-धीरे कन्नड़ को हाशिये से महाकाव्य के केंद्र तक पहुँचा दिया।

cast: Ranna, Jewel of the Jain Poets
panels.shot: final contemplative medium shot of Ranna looking out over the Kannada countryside, manuscript closed in his hands
panels.action: Ranna stands on a hill crest at dusk, a rolled palm-leaf manuscript held gently in both hands, as he looks out over fields, villages and temple spires, the sky glowing softly above the Kannada land he has given a new voice.

dialogue.text: Ranna’s journey shows that a language grows when poets trust it with greatness, and that when faith, power and art meet in living tongues, they leave echoes louder than any empire’s stone.

i18n.hi: रण्णा की यात्रा बताती है कि भाषा तब बढ़ती है जब कवि उस पर महानता का भरोसा रखें, और जब विश्वास, सत्ता और कला ज़िंदा ज़बानों में मिलें, तो उनकी गूँज किसी भी साम्राज्य की पत्थर की दीवारों से ज़्यादा दूर तक जाती है।

title_i18n.hi: रण्णा को मिली कन्नड़ की आवाज़

subtitle_i18n.en: How Jain courts forged an epic tongue in stone and song
subtitle_i18n.hi: जैन दरबारों ने पत्थर और गीत में गढ़ी वीर कन्नड़
